chapter-15-extras.note: Dictionary form of あいます (aimasu, "meet", Lesson 9). Regular 1: the い before ます becomes う.
chapter-15-extras.reviewNote: Verb dictionary-form batch (2026-09). あいます was carded in Lesson 9 with no dictionary form anywhere in the deck; the book never prints this one.

chapter-15-extras.note: Dictionary form of あげます (agemasu, "give", Lesson 14). Regular 2, so ます simply becomes る. Lesson 15's grammar names あげます in its own list of the Regular 2 verbs taught up to that point, precisely so this form can be derived.
chapter-15-extras.reviewNote: Verb dictionary-form batch (2026-09). Recovery, not an invention: Lesson 15 GRAMMAR 2 enumerates あげます among the Regular 2 verbs introduced through Lesson 14, and the dictionary form was never carded.

chapter-15-extras.note: Dictionary form of あります (arimasu, Lesson 12), and it covers every sense this deck teaches that verb in: "be, exist", "have", and "there is, takes place". Regular 1: the り before ます becomes る. Its animate partner います (imasu, "be, exist") has the dictionary form いる (iru).
chapter-15-extras.reviewNote: Verb dictionary-form batch (2026-09). あります is carded three times across Lessons 12, 14 and 16 with three senses; one dictionary-form card serves all three, so the note names them rather than splitting the card.

chapter-15-extras.note: Dictionary form of おくります (okurimasu, "send", Lesson 9). Regular 1: the り before ます becomes る, the same change as のります → のる.
chapter-15-extras.reviewNote: Verb dictionary-form batch (2026-09). おくります was carded in Lesson 9 with no dictionary form anywhere in the deck.

chapter-15-extras.note: Dictionary form of かります (karimasu, "borrow", Lesson 14). It looks like a Regular 1 verb, since り sits before ます, but it is Regular 2: ます becomes る and the り stays, giving かりる and never かる. Lesson 15's grammar lists it among the Regular 2 verbs taught so far for exactly this reason. Contrast かします (kashimasu, "lend"), which really is Regular 1 and gives かす (kasu).
chapter-15-extras.reviewNote: Verb dictionary-form batch (2026-09). Recovery: Lesson 15 GRAMMAR 2 enumerates かります among the Regular 2 verbs introduced through Lesson 14, and the dictionary form was never carded. The R1-lookalike trap is the whole reason the book names it.

chapter-15-extras.note: Dictionary form of くれます (kuremasu, "give (to me)", Lesson 14). Regular 2: ます becomes る. Pairs with あげる (ageru, "give") the same way くれます pairs with あげます — くれる is used when the thing comes toward you.
chapter-15-extras.reviewNote: Verb dictionary-form batch (2026-09). くれます was carded in Lesson 14 with no dictionary form anywhere in the deck.

chapter-9-extras.hint: the word for your own child, and the general word for a child
chapter-9-extras.note: Used for your own child, opposite おこさん (okosan) for someone else's — the same humble/honorific split as ちち (chichi, "my father") against おとうさん (otōsan). こども is also the ordinary general word for "child" in any other context. こ (ko, "child") from Lesson 13 is the shorter root that builds おんなのこ (onna no ko, "girl") and おとこのこ (otoko no ko, "boy").
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Family batch (2026-09). Book-sourced but taught later: Lesson 24's WORD POWER family table. Glossed "(My) child" rather than "Child" because こ already carries "Child" in Lesson 13 — see the collision rule in card-authoring-rules.md. Hint added because the gloss narrows a word that is also general.

chapter-9-extras.note: Someone else's child — for your own, use こども (kodomo). Same pattern as おとうさん (otōsan) against ちち (chichi) in this lesson.
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Family batch (2026-09). Book-sourced but taught later: Lesson 24's WORD POWER family table.

chapter-9-extras.note: Used for your own son; for someone else's, use むすこさん (musukosan).
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Family batch (2026-09). Book-sourced but taught later: Lesson 24's WORD POWER family table.

chapter-9-extras.note: Someone else's son — for your own, use むすこ (musuko). The honorific here is the plain さん (san) suffix from Lesson 1, not a ご- prefix.
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Family batch (2026-09). Book-sourced but taught later: Lesson 24's WORD POWER family table.

chapter-9-extras.note: Used for your own daughter; for someone else's, use おじょうさん (ojōsan).

chapter-9-extras.note: Someone else's daughter — for your own, use むすめ (musume). むすめさん (musumesan) works too; おじょうさん is the politer of the two and also serves as a polite word for a young woman generally.
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Family batch (2026-09). Book-sourced but taught later: Lesson 24's WORD POWER family table, which lists おじょうさん／むすめさん as alternatives. Carded as おじょうさん with むすめさん in the note rather than as two cards, to avoid a third "(Another person's) daughter" gloss collision.

chapter-9-extras.note: Japanese has no single word for "brother": age is built into the noun, so あに is specifically an older brother and おとうと (otōto) a younger one. Used for your own; for someone else's, use おにいさん (oniisan).
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Family batch (2026-09). Book-sourced but taught later: Lesson 24's WORD POWER family table.

chapter-9-extras.note: Someone else's older brother — for your own, use あに (ani). It is also how you address your own older brother directly, the way English uses a name.
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Family batch (2026-09). Book-sourced but taught later: Lesson 24's WORD POWER family table.

chapter-9-extras.note: Specifically an older sister; a younger one is いもうと (imōto). Used for your own; for someone else's, use おねえさん (onēsan).
chapter-9-extras.reviewNote: Family batch (2026-09). Book-sourced but taught later: Lesson 24's WORD POWER family table.

chapter-9-extras.note: The collective word for siblings of either sex, which is what you use when the age order does not matter and あに (ani) or いもうと (imōto) would be too specific. For someone else's, use ごきょうだい (gokyōdai).

chapter-9-extras.note: ご (go, honorific prefix) + きょうだい (kyōdai, "brothers and sisters"), built exactly like ごかぞく (gokazoku) in this lesson. Used about someone else's siblings, never your own.
